note: Section 17: performance at PRIMARY POINT B (ctx=180000, SmolLM2-360M, real GTX 1650 Vulkan, --gpu-layers all).

product_whole_cache_q5.method: membrane-run --kv q5 --gpu-layers all --ctx 180000 --gen-tokens 32, prompt 'The largest planet in our solar system is', 7 fresh runs, real product performance.prompt_tok_per_s / generation_tok_per_s fields
product_whole_cache_q5.note_on_variance: prompt_tok_per_s has a visibly high first-run outlier (240.35 on run 1 vs 300-369 on runs 2-7), consistent with one-time GPU/driver warmup (shader compilation, first-allocation cache-miss) rather than genuine steady-state variance; not discarded as an outlier here, reported as measured.

research_mixed_top8_vs_whole_q5_wall_clo.method: membrane-kv-sequential-compare --mode compare (teacher-forced pass + a free-running pass, i.e. MORE total decode work per invocation than membrane-run's single pass), --ctx 180000 --gpu-layers all, 7 fresh runs each, external wall-clock via the POSIX `time` utility -- this is NOT directly comparable to the product prompt/generation_tok_per_s numbers above (different code path, does two passes not one); reported only as an internal, apples-to-apples Q5-vs-mixed comparison using the identical tool for both.
research_mixed_top8_vs_whole_q5_wall_clo.caveat: --kv mixed has no product CLI exposure (by design, this phase must not expose it), so no product-level tok/s number exists for mixed; this research-tool wall-clock timing is the closest available like-for-like signal.

conclusion: No material performance difference between whole-Q5 and mixed top-8 at PRIMARY POINT B (within run-to-run noise, whole-Q5's mean is skewed slightly high by one first-run warmup outlier; medians are within 2%). Performance does not favor or penalize either config meaningfully here, consistent with Section 17's instruction not to let performance dominate the decision -- it doesn't, because there is nothing here for it to dominate.
